DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Forty a Day, Then Double

STS-HS11-L3-13001400-HSALG2-ARA-API-02 • HS Math Algebra II Grade 11 • Comparing Two Functions in Different Representations
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Every summer from the 1920s, thousands of Filipino workers called Alaskeros sailed north to the salmon canneries and came home in the fall with a season of pay and a season of numbers. Some families kept those numbers in a ledger, written down day by day. Others painted them as a curve on canvas so you could see a whole season in one look. The same season can be a table of numbers or a shape on a grid, and each one shows you something the other hides.
One record adds the same amount every day and the other doubles, so which one wins, and does it win right away?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amihan doing?
Look at the picture. Say what Amihan is doing and why she is doing it in two complete sentences. Use an exact verb, not a general verb like doing or making.
2
What is Bayani holding?
Look at the picture. Say what Bayani is holding and why he holds it open so the others can see it in two complete sentences. Name the object exactly, not with a general word like thing or stuff.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say what the teacher is doing and why he works so carefully with the old tin in two complete sentences. Use an exact verb, not a general verb like fixing or working.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say what place this is and how you know in two complete sentences. Name two different things in the picture that prove it, not general words like stuff.
5
Tell me what you see on the hanging chart.
Look at the picture. Say one thing on the hanging chart and what it tells you about that season in two complete sentences. Use exact words for what the chart shows, not general words like stuff or things.
6
Tell me about what Dalisay is wearing.
Look at the picture. Say what Dalisay is wearing and why that kind of clothing fits this place in two complete sentences. Name the color and the kind of clothing exactly.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
